caption: In a chit fund, 20 members paying Rs 5,000 a month build a Rs 1,00,000 pot, and one member takes it home each month. The foreman can legally take up to 7% of the pot every month, so only ever join a registered chit with a written agreement.

pages.name: cover
pages.sub:
How they work
and why they go wrong.
pages.title:
CHIT
FUNDS

pages.body: Members pay a fixed amount every month into one pot. Each month, one member takes the pot home.
pages.heading: A group savings pot.
pages.name: idea

pages.body: Each month the pot goes to the biggest discount. The discount funds the fee and a dividend.
pages.heading: Who takes it first?
pages.name: auction
pages.note: Discounts are capped by law, usually at 30% of the pot.

pages.body: The organiser takes a fee from every monthly pot. The law caps it at 7% of the chit value.
pages.heading: The foreman's cut.
pages.name: cost
pages.note: At the maximum fee every month. Many foremen charge less.

pages.body: One question decides if the law protects you.

groups.items: State registered. Foreman posts a security deposit. Fees capped.
groups.title: REGISTERED CHIT

groups.items: No registration, no deposit, no cap. If the foreman vanishes, you have no remedy.
groups.title: UNREGISTERED CHIT

pages.heading: Registered or not?
pages.name: divide

pages.body: A chit fund can work as forced savings. Only join one that passes all three checks.
pages.heading: Three checks first.

items: Registered with the Registrar of Chits
inner.title: Join only if all three are yes

pages.name: checks
pages.note: Never join a chit run only on WhatsApp with no paperwork.
